tools.title: Gable & Rake Wall Stud Calculator
tools.desc: Length of every stud beneath a sloping top plate
tools.formula: height(x) = start + x × pitch/12; cut = height − plate deduction
tools.example: 144 in wall, 96 in start height, 6:12 gives end height 168 in before plates
tools.limit: Geometry only; no structural approval

tools.title: Wall Framing with Doors & Windows
tools.desc: Plot full-height studs and reference king/jack centers around up to three door or window openings, each with its own sill and height.
tools.formula: Use OC grid outside opening side packs; jack centers = opening edges ± studWidth/2; king centers = edges ± 1.5×studWidth; rough opening top = sill + height.
tools.example: 120 in wall, 16 in OC, 1.5 in studs, opening from 32 to 68 in, 80 in high: six unaffected grid centers and four opening-side reference centers.
tools.limit: Reference geometry only: opening elevations are not precut member lengths. Headers, cripples, sill framing, plate deductions, structural sizing and code compliance require separate design.

guidance.heading: Door and window elevations share a floor datum
guidance.text: Set sill to 0 for a door. For a window, enter its sill elevation and opening height separately. The cutout shows the rough opening only; headers, cripple studs and trim are not generated.

guidance.heading: Jack and king positions are center marks
guidance.text: Each jack and king reference center is calculated from a clear opening edge and the stud width. Regular on-center members inside these side packs are omitted. Verify actual stock, rough-opening tolerances, and local requirements before cutting.

tools.title: Deck Board & Gap Calculator
tools.desc: Number of straight decking rows and last rip width
tools.formula: rows = ceil((width+gap)/(board+gap)); last width = width−(rows−1)(board+gap)
tools.example: 120 in at 5.5 in board + 0.125 in gap gives 22 rows and 1.875 in final rip
tools.limit: No joist load design or joint optimization

tools.title: Baluster & Spindle Spacing
tools.desc: Equal clear gaps and individual baluster coordinates
tools.formula: n = ceil((opening−maxGap)/(width+maxGap)); equal gap = (opening−n×width)/(n+1)
tools.example: 96 in clear, 1.5 in faces, 4 in maximum: 17 balusters, 3.9167 in gaps
tools.limit: Not a safety-code compliance certificate

tools.title: Common Rafter & Birdsmouth Reference
tools.desc: Ridge-adjusted rafter line, overhang and birdsmouth seat-notch depth reference
tools.formula: adjustedRun=run−ridge/2; slope=pitch/12; slopeLength=run×√(1+slope²); notchNormalDepth=seat×sin(atan(slope)); remainingDepth=stockDepth−notchNormalDepth
tools.example: 120 in run at 6:12 yields rise 60 in and reference line 134.164 in
tools.limit: Seat length is a horizontal cut-reference, not a certified birdsmouth or heel. Notch thickness is measured normal to the rafter's long edges; stock grade, bearing width, local code and roof loads must be checked independently. Diagram is a schematic, never a 1:1 saw template.

guidance.heading: Measure the run and ridge reference
guidance.text: Measure the horizontal run to the ridge centerline, then enter the actual ridge board thickness. The tool subtracts half that thickness before computing the bearing-to-ridge line length. Roof pitch is the vertical rise over 12 inches of horizontal run, not the angle of the saw blade.

guidance.heading: Differentiate seat length and notch depth
guidance.text: The seat input is a horizontal projection along the bearing line. The vertical rise across that span is seat × pitch/12. The depth of that wedge measured perpendicular to the long rafter edges is seat × sin(arctan(pitch/12)). It is NOT the same as the full rafter stock depth or a bearing-capacity verification.

guidance.heading: Check the support and eave separately
guidance.text: The wall bearing point and overhang tail are listed separately in the measurement schedule. The line from ridge to bearing excludes the eave extension; the total slope distance includes it. Ridge-to-bearing and ridge-to-eave dimensions use the same pitch but must not be confused.

guidance.heading: Do not cut from this SVG at paper scale
guidance.text: Confirm the actual plumb/seat layout using a framing square and reference faces on scrap lumber. Ridge connection, roof loads, seat bearing, notch limits and local requirements are outside this geometry model. The diagram is deliberately not a certified full-size template.

tools.title: Crown Molding Compound Cuts
tools.desc: Compound angle magnitudes and explicit inside/outside, left/right illustrative references with a typed CSV angle schedule
tools.formula: Geometric flat-saw angle magnitudes only: miter = atan(sin(spring)/tan(included wall corner/2)); bevel = asin(cos(spring)×cos(included wall corner/2)). An illustrative plan-view sign changes with inside/outside and left/right selection; this sign is NOT a calibrated saw-control setting.
tools.example: 38° spring angle with a 90° included wall corner gives a 31.62° miter magnitude and a 33.86° bevel magnitude. Inside/outside and left/right change only the illustrative plan sign, not these geometric magnitudes.
tools.limit: Angles are idealized geometric magnitudes under the stated spring/included-corner convention. The signed plan view is illustrative ONLY and must not be used as a prescribed miter-saw left/right, flip, face-up/down or fence placement. Saw brand scales, crown orientation, inside/outside cut direction, relief/back bevel, joint tolerance and physical jig settings require independent hands-on scrap verification.

guidance.heading: Use the included wall angle and the stated spring convention
guidance.text: The entered corner angle is measured between adjacent walls on the selected side. The spring angle is treated as the nominal crown-to-wall spring convention used in the displayed formulas. Check the actual profile and installation orientation before using the computed magnitudes.

guidance.heading: Separate angle magnitudes from saw direction
guidance.text: Miter magnitude and bevel magnitude remain the same when you choose left/right or inside/outside. The optional signed miter only changes an illustrative plan-view sketch and CSV reference. It is NOT a saw rotation command; real hand, crown orientation and tool setup vary.

guidance.heading: Export angles with unambiguous units
guidance.text: The angle schedule includes the selected corner type and piece hand, spring and wall angle, both magnitudes and the signed illustration angle, all in degrees. Switching in/mm does not change any angles.

guidance.heading: Cut a verified sample before processing stock
guidance.text: Confirm the actual saw, crown bedding, surface face, fence orientation and corner geometry with scrap pieces. This tool does not certify safe saw operation, fit, hold-down methods or cutting accuracy.

tools.title: Soffit Drop & Eave Section
tools.desc: Datum-labelled eave section: roof fall, rafter underside, lining and signed fascia adjustment with a proportional cross-section
tools.formula: Roof-top fall = horizontal eave projection × pitch/12. Vertical separation of parallel roof faces = rafter normal depth × √(1+(pitch/12)²). Finished soffit reference drop from the wall rafter-top datum = roof fall + vertical rafter separation + lining vertical thickness + signed fascia adjustment (down positive).
tools.example: At 24 in projection and 6:12 pitch, roof-top fall is 12 in. With a 5.5 in normal rafter depth, 0.5 in lining and zero offset, the vertical rafter separation is 6.1492 in and the finished reference drop is 18.6492 in.
tools.limit: Reference datum is the TOP of the rafter at the wall; positive vertical values point DOWN. Rafter depth is perpendicular to its slope; lining thickness is specified vertically; fascia adjustment is a signed downward-positive additive offset. The diagram models these reference surfaces, not eave framing, structural load, material fastening or a 1:1 cutting template. Actual fascia/soffit assemblies may use different planes and must be field checked.

guidance.heading: Start from a defined wall reference datum
guidance.text: The zero-height line is the top face of the rafter at the wall reference. The nominal pitch fall is measured vertically from this datum to the top rafter surface at the outer eave, for the horizontal projection entered.

guidance.heading: Convert normal rafter depth into a vertical face difference
guidance.text: The rafter depth is measured square to the roof slope, not vertically. Parallel surfaces separated by normal stock depth d have vertical difference d×√(1+slope²) at the same horizontal station. At a 6:12 pitch this exceeds d by about 11.8%.

guidance.heading: Apply lining thickness and the signed fascia datum separately
guidance.text: The finished soffit reference adds the stated vertical lining thickness and the signed fascia adjustment to the eave underside drop. Positive adjustment means farther down; a negative adjustment raises the reference. The exact physical reference plane of a real fascia/soffit assembly must be checked on site.

guidance.heading: Use dimensioned numbers, not the printed SVG as a cutting template
guidance.text: The line drawing illustrates the same numeric datum relationships shown in the results and the two-row CSV. It does not dimension the roof from framing grade, promise local code suitability, provide vertical load-bearing recommendations or certify paper-scale cuts.

tools.title: Kerf Bending Layout
tools.desc: Kerf-bending flat-stock trial plan with continuous-web and nonoverlap checks, saw-mouth extents and a depth-profile drawing
tools.formula: Developed reference arc length = radius×angle (radians). Idealized closure per cut = 2×atan(kerf width/(2×cut depth)); cut depth = stock thickness−retained web. Proposed cuts = ceil(target angle/estimated closure); center spacing = reference arc length/count; clear land = spacing−kerf width. Continuous web and clear land must both be positive.
tools.example: 100 mm reference radius and 90° target gives 157.08 mm developed arc. For a 0.75 in stock with 0.125 in continuous web and 0.125 in saw kerf, 8 proposed cuts give about 19.63 mm pitch; the idealized model does not guarantee final wood curvature.
tools.limit: Geometry-only idealized slit closure, NOT a verified wood-bending, neutral-axis or springback model. Radius is a user-selected reference arc, not a guaranteed finished inside/outer radius. Retained web must be positive; flat kerf mouths must remain separate. Wood species, grain, fatigue, tear-out, saw accuracy and actual bending require scrap trials. SVG/print are scaled schematics, NOT certified 1:1 saw templates.

guidance.heading: Reference arc does not guarantee finished bend radius
guidance.text: The flat layout length is reference radius × bend angle in radians. Real curvature depends on material and the retained continuous web; the neutral axis and finished inside/outer radius are not calculated.

guidance.heading: Preserve a connected web and separate kerf mouths
guidance.text: Each cut stops at the continuous remaining web. Zero web would sever the board and is rejected. If adjacent kerf mouth openings touch or overlap on the flat stock, the suggested layout is rejected instead of generating unusable cut coordinates.

guidance.heading: Distinguish closure estimate from intended turn
guidance.text: Idealized maximum closure per cut is 2×atan(kerf width/(2×cut depth)). The number of cuts rounds up to meet the requested angle; planned average turn per cut = target angle/count, which can be smaller than the estimated maximum closure. Neither predicts springback.

guidance.heading: Inspect the slot profile and trial on scrap
guidance.text: The schedule exports each cut center, two slot mouth edges, depth, retained wood and maximum closure estimate. The flat-stock SVG shows cut mouths above the continuous web and is not a real-scale cutting template. Verify all dimensions and bending behavior on sacrificial stock first.

tools.title: Wainscoting Panel Layout
tools.desc: Equally sized panels between margins and gaps
tools.formula: panel width = (wall−2×margin−(panels−1)×gap)/panels
tools.example: 120 in wall, 5 panels, 3 in margins, 2 in gaps: 21.2 in panels
tools.limit: Doors, skirting and stile dimensions excluded

tools.title: Straight Stair Calculator
tools.desc: Riser count, rise, tread count and run
tools.formula: risers=ceil(rise/desired); actual rise=rise/risers; treads=risers−1
tools.example: 105 in / 7.5 in ⇒ 14 risers and 13 treads
tools.limit: Geometry, not a stair-code certificate

tools.title: Rise & Run Slope Converter
tools.desc: Rise/run, slope angle and hypotenuse
tools.formula: slope=rise/run; angle=atan(slope); length=hypot(rise,run)
tools.limit: Run must be nonzero

tools.title: Deck Material Estimator
tools.desc: Rectangular deck board rows, final rip, joist-center butt seams, conservative supported stock segments and printable geometry
tools.formula: Rows = ceil((coverage+gap)/(board face width+gap)); final rip = coverage−(rows−1)×(face width+gap). With given joist center references (0, OC, …, end), each board segment ends at the farthest joist center reachable within purchased stock length, unless the final deck end is reachable. Every supported piece consumes one stock board; no offcut reuse or seam staggering.
tools.example: For a 120 × 144 in deck using 5.5 in boards and 0.125 in gaps, 16 in joist centers and 100 in stock: 22 rows with a 1.875 in final rip each receive a 96 in and 48 in segment, joined at the 96 in joist center reference. This gives 44 stock boards before allowance, not a 100 in/44 in unsupported joint.
tools.limit: Rectangular straight-deck reference geometry only. Segment butt joints are constrained to entered joist CENTERLINES, not validated bearing widths, joint reinforcement, double-joist blocking or fastening. All rows use identical, UNSTAGGERED joints as a conservative reference, not an approved construction pattern. No offcut reuse, structural span approval, load rating, end gap, board defects, ledger design or footing calculations.

guidance.heading: Boards and joist reference grid
guidance.text: Deck width runs across parallel decking rows; deck length runs along them. Joist centers begin at zero, follow your chosen OC spacing and end with a potentially shorter last bay. Enter actual face width and purchased stock length, not nominal lumber sizes.

guidance.heading: Every butt seam must have a reference center
guidance.text: Unlike simple stock-length division, this calculator places every intermediate board end at the furthest joist center that can be reached within one purchased board. If there is no such joist center and stock will not span to the deck end, the tool rejects the layout rather than inventing an unsupported butt seam. The SVG marks each proposed seam and the CSV exports butt-joint coordinates.

guidance.heading: Layout reference, NOT a fastening or stagger plan
guidance.text: The reference repeats the same seams across all rows and does not stagger joints. A single joist centerline does not establish sufficient edge bearing for two board ends; joist width, double-joist/blocking support, end gaps, fastening, local rules and safe maximum joist span must be reviewed separately. Counts are conservative without offcut reuse.

tools.title: Segmented Bowl Ring Calculator
tools.desc: Finished ring chord and half-miter dimensions with a per-piece segment schedule for all rings
tools.formula: Half-miter = 180°/segments; chordOuter = outsideDiameter×sin(π/segments); chordInner = insideDiameter×sin(π/segments); radialDepth = (outsideDiameter−insideDiameter)/2. Every segment of every ring is listed.
tools.example: A 12 in outside diameter, 8 in inside diameter, 12-piece ring needs 15° miters, 3.10583 in outer chords, 2.07055 in inner chords, and 2 in radial depth. Three identical rings yield 36 listed pieces.
tools.limit: All rings are treated as identical, with finished diameters and trapezoid wedges. Chords do not include blade kerf, joint allowance, stock-blank oversize, grain orientation, ring staggering or glue/lathing waste. Validate real stock and saw setup with a scrap test.

guidance.heading: Chord length versus segment stock
guidance.text: Outer and inner chords are straight edge-to-edge distances on the finished ring circumference. A full segment has two radial end faces. These finished dimensions are not the minimum raw stock length once kerf and saw setup are considered.

guidance.heading: Review the full segment schedule
guidance.text: Every ring and segment has an individual row containing its angular interval, miter angle, outer chord, inner chord and radial depth. CSV angles are exported as degrees; lengths follow the selected measurement unit.

guidance.heading: Important lathe and assembly exclusions
guidance.text: This calculator does not optimize waste or design glue joints. Repeating identical rings is a geometric convention, not a verified bowl profile or recommended build plan; confirm blank dimensions, material grain, glue and safe lathe methods independently.

tools.title: Roof Pitch in Degrees & Percent
tools.desc: Convert 12-inch roof pitch to angles and rise
tools.formula: angle=atan(pitch/12); grade=100×pitch/12; rise=run×pitch/12
tools.limit: Roof geometry only

tools.title: Equal Center Spacing
tools.desc: Place points exactly between two end offsets
tools.formula: pitch=(length−left−right)/(n−1); n=1 is centered
tools.example: 1000 mm and 6 endpoint centers ⇒ 200 mm intervals
tools.limit: Offsets are to centers, not item edges

tools.title: Hip Rafter Line Geometry
tools.desc: Plan diagonal, roof rise and three-dimensional hip line
tools.formula: plan=hypot(x,y); rise=y×pitch/12; line=hypot(plan,rise)
tools.example: 120 by 120 in plan and 6:12 rise gives plan 169.706 in
tools.limit: No load or compound-cut structural sizing

tools.title: Hip Roof Sheet Layout Calculator
tools.desc: Divide an equal-pitch rectangular hip roof into four actual slope-face panels, inspect clipped sheet layouts and export cut coordinates.
tools.formula: Slope factor = sqrt(1+(pitch/12)^2). Each hip plane becomes a local triangle or trapezoid. Clip its outline to every sheet rectangle and sum the resulting polygon areas.
tools.example: For a flat 192 × 96 in hip-roof footprint and 96 × 48 in sheets, area requires at least four sheets, but a separate-sheet-per-cut layout uses six positions.
tools.limit: Geometry of an equal-pitch rectangular four-plane roof only. Sheets are placed in straight eave-origin rows, without seam gaps, staggering, offcut reuse, fastening or building-code checks. Plans are scaled schematics and NOT certified full-size cutting templates.

guidance.heading: Sheet orientation and the four local axes
guidance.text: The default places the long sheet edge parallel to each roof eave and the short edge up the slope. Rotate by 90 degrees with the sheet direction control. The (eave, uphill) coordinates in the table restart at each of the four roof planes.

guidance.heading: Cut polygon coordinates
guidance.text: For each listed sheet, cut vertices are measured from that sheet's lower-left local corner. The colored rooftop plan view projects exactly those clipped polygons into a bird's-eye diagram. The CSV preserves all row coordinates for bench-side checking.

guidance.heading: No offcut reuse or engineered joint layout
guidance.text: A cut sheet may contain a small triangular remnant that this conservative count discards. This is not optimized stock nesting, a structural sheathing schedule, or a substitute for checking fastening, edge setbacks and actual cut tolerances.

tools.title: Wall Stud Count & Layout
tools.desc: Regular vertical stud centers and last-end placement
tools.formula: positions=0, OC multiples below L, and exactly one far end
tools.example: 120 in at 16 in spacing gives 9 locations
tools.limit: Opening studs require dedicated framing tool

tools.title: Shelf Spacing & Drill Marks
tools.desc: Equalize shelf clearances between reserved top/bottom minimums and output each shelf's bottom/top face coordinates
tools.formula: Free height = interior height − shelves×thickness − top reserve − bottom reserve. Shared base gap = free height/(shelves+1). Actual bottom opening = bottom reserve+base gap; actual top opening = top reserve+base gap; all between-shelf gaps = base gap.
tools.example: A 40 in interior with three 1 in shelves and 2 in extra bottom and 1 in extra top reserves leaves a shared 8.5 in base gap; actual bottom clear opening is 10.5 in, actual top clear opening 9.5 in.
tools.limit: Top and bottom inputs are extra minimum-reserve clearances, not the final visible openings. Finished shelf faces and clear gaps follow the supplied interior height and actual material thickness. No shelf-load, fixing, sag or material tolerance assessment.

guidance.heading: Reserved versus actual end clearances
guidance.text: The top and bottom inputs reserve minimum space. Remaining free height is spread across all spaces. Actual bottom clearance = bottom reserve + shared gap; actual top clearance = top reserve + shared gap. If you need the end openings to be exact values, verify the calculated final openings before construction.

guidance.heading: Measure bottom and top faces from the case floor
guidance.text: Every schedule row gives the shelf's bottom and upper surfaces, clear opening below, and clear opening above. All positions reference the inside bottom of the case; board thickness and spacing share the same model.

guidance.heading: Loads and mounting are not sized
guidance.text: This is a geometry-only shelf spacing calculator. It does not recommend material spans, deflection limits, screw spacing, load ratings, wall anchors or fastening methods.

tools.title: Gable Roof Area Calculator
tools.desc: Two planar roof areas using width, pitch and overhangs
tools.formula: line=hypot(halfspan,halfspan×pitch/12); area=2×line×effective length
tools.example: A symmetric gable has two matching roof planes
tools.limit: Dormers, valleys and waste excluded

tools.title: Square Layout Diagonal Checker
tools.desc: Ideal diagonal and deviations from measured diagonals
tools.formula: ideal=hypot(width,length); compare diagonals with ideal
tools.example: 3×4 ft rectangle has 5 ft ideal diagonal
tools.limit: Equal diagonals alone do not prove squareness

tools.title: Diagonal Brace Calculator
tools.desc: Brace diagonal centerline and angle
tools.formula: length=hypot(width,height)−2×setback; angle=atan2(height,width)
tools.example: 3 ft × 4 ft ⇒ 5 ft brace reference
tools.limit: No end joinery or load calculation

tools.title: Hole Spacing Drilling Guide
tools.desc: Drilling centers and hole-edge coordinates, measured end margins, inter-hole clear material and proportional circle layout
tools.formula: Center pitch = (stock length−2×end center setback)/(hole count−1); drilled hole edges = center±hole diameter/2; inter-hole clear material = center pitch−diameter; end material margin = end center setback−diameter/2.
tools.example: On a 100 mm board with four 5 mm holes, centered 5 mm in from either end, pitch is 30 mm, hole-to-hole clear material is 25 mm, and the solid end margin is 2.5 mm. Hole edges from the left are 2.5–7.5, 32.5–37.5, 62.5–67.5 and 92.5–97.5 mm.
tools.limit: Hole center setback is NOT edge-to-edge material clearance. Hole circles and interval spacing depict longitudinal geometry only; actual board face width, transverse edge clearance, drill-bit runout, grain tear-out, tolerances, clamping, workholding, fastener loads and material strength are not checked. Touching holes may produce 0 clear material. SVG is illustrative, never a 1:1 drilling template.

guidance.heading: Center setback versus remaining end material
guidance.text: Enter the distance from each stock end to the first or last hole center. The actual wood remaining between the hole edge and stock end is setback minus half the drill diameter. Both are explicitly computed, so a 5 mm center setback on a 5 mm diameter hole leaves 2.5 mm of end wood.

guidance.heading: Check spacing between drilled edges
guidance.text: The center pitch is not the wood thickness between holes. Clear material between neighboring holes is the center pitch minus the full hole diameter; the calculator rejects negative clear material where round holes would overlap along the board.

guidance.heading: Review exact hole edges and local CSV
guidance.text: The schedule lists each center coordinate and the hole's left and right extents, its diameter and the material clearance to the previous hole. SVG circles have a consistent horizontal and vertical geometric scale within the diagram. The drawing does not verify perpendicular edge clearance, material tear-out or drill accuracy.

tools.title: Straight Stair Stringer Cut Reference
tools.desc: Straight stringer nominal tread/riser profile with exact SVG vertices, distinct notch pitch-line and floor datum diagonal, bottom cut correction and nominal throat
tools.formula: Riser height = total finished-floor rise/risers; treads=risers−1; horizontal run=treads×tread run. The notch pitch line from first tread at (0,riser height) to upper landing at (run,total rise) measures hypot(run,treads×riser height). The different floor datum diagonal measures hypot(run,total rise) and is NOT a stringer cut length. Notch penetration=step rise×tread run/hypot(step rise,tread run); nominal throat=board normal depth−notch penetration; bottom trim=step rise−tread thickness+additional lower finish.
tools.example: 105 in between finished floors, 14 risers and 10 in tread run yield 7.5 in risers, 13 treads, 130 in horizontal run, 162.5 in first-tread-to-landing notch pitch reference and about 167.1 in floor-to-floor diagonal (not a board cut length). With 1.5 in tread stock and no later lower finish, bottom trim reference is 6 in.
tools.limit: Nominal straight-stair *reference* only. The floor-to-floor diagonal is NOT a stringer cut length or stock length. The first riser nominal profile is distinct from the bottom trim that compensates for the tread/floor finish. SVG uses nominal step vertices and is NOT a 1:1 saw template or actual stock outline. Actual top/bottom bearing, nosing, throat code limits, fasteners, total stock, fit and structural safety require site verification.

guidance.heading: Separate the two diagonals
guidance.text: The nominal notch pitch line runs from the top of the first riser to the top landing, with rise equal to the 13 inter-riser steps. The floor-to-floor chord starts at the lower datum and has a different angle and length. Neither should automatically be ordered or cut as a raw timber board length.

guidance.heading: Review the exact nominal step-coordinate diagram
guidance.text: The SVG now draws from the same (x,height) vertices generated by the engine: 14 riser segments, with 13 horizontal tread segments. The diagram's dashed pitch reference and floor chord are distinct. It is a scaled schematic, not a physical full-size pattern.

guidance.heading: Keep the bottom trim separate from nominal riser geometry
guidance.text: For conventional tread installation, bottom layout cut height = one nominal riser − finished tread thickness + any lower finish installed after the stringer. This is an end-trim reference only; it does not shift all nominal riser elevations. The diagram marks that bottom reference independently.

guidance.heading: Nominal throat is not an engineering rating
guidance.text: Stock normal depth less step notch penetration gives a nominal remaining throat. Capacity depends on wood grade, defects, fasteners, local code and actual support details; do not treat the geometric clearance or illustrated diagonal as engineered approval.

tools.title: Roof Sheathing Calculator
tools.desc: Rectangular single-plane sheathing layout with true sloped depth, clipped edge sheets and a complete cut schedule
tools.formula: True sloped depth = roof plan width × sqrt(1+(pitch/12)^2); clip a grid of stock sheets to the roof plane; purchase count = occupied sheet positions plus optional allowance.
tools.example: A flat 110 × 70 in roof plane with 96 × 48 in sheets needs four sheet positions, including three edge cuts, before allowance.
tools.limit: Single rectangular roof plane only; eave-origin grid without seam gaps, staggering, offcut reuse, fastening, bearing or structural compliance checks. SVG is a scaled schematic, not a certified 1:1 pattern.

guidance.heading: Understand eave and uphill dimensions
guidance.text: Roof plan width measures the horizontal uphill run; plan length measures the eave. The pitched run is converted to its true sloped surface length before positioning each sheet.

guidance.heading: Review every sheet cut
guidance.text: The diagram shows the single plane in flat sloped-surface coordinates. Eave start and slope start locate each sheet from the lower-left eave corner. Cut along and cut uphill are the cut dimensions, all exported in CSV.

guidance.heading: Conservative purchasing, not a fastening plan
guidance.text: Every occupied position consumes one stock sheet without offcut reuse. Compare sheet orientations to reduce the conservative count. Allowance applies to occupied sheets, not the area lower bound; confirm real fastening, seam and support details separately.

tools.title: Fence Post Layout Calculator
tools.desc: Fit non-overlapping straight-fence posts across an explicit end-center-to-end-center run and list each usable clear bay
tools.formula: Bays = ceil(end-post center distance / maximum OC spacing); actual OC = center distance/bays; clear gap = actual OC−actual post face width. Impossible overlapping or touching posts are rejected.
tools.example: 100 ft between end-post centers at a maximum 8 ft OC uses 13 bays and 14 posts, 92.3077 in actual OC. With 3.5 in post faces, each clear bay is 88.8077 in.
tools.limit: Length means distance between first and last post centers, NOT outside-to-outside fence length. Ends extend half a post width beyond those centers. Layout is a straight-line reference; footing, grade, wind, code, panels and gate loads are not assessed.

guidance.heading: Set the correct end-to-end datum
guidance.text: Measure from the center of the first post to the center of the last post. The outside faces of these two end posts extend by half a post width at either end; do not confuse the centerline run with the overall finished outside length.

guidance.heading: No negative clear bays
guidance.text: The calculator shortens the specified maximum on-center spacing to fit equal bays. If the resulting spacing is no greater than the actual post face width, the calculation is rejected instead of reporting negative usable opening.

guidance.heading: This is layout geometry, not a fence specification
guidance.text: The listed center coordinates and clear bay widths do not establish safe posts, foundations, panel support, gate spacing or local-code compliance. Check local requirements and actual material faces.
